correctness.rationale: For H=J(P) with finite Gödel dual P a rooted forest, sigma(H)=#{(a,b):a→b=b} multiplies over components. Adding a least root to forest algebra B of size m gives |H|=m+1, sigma(H)=m+1+sigma(B), and failures Δ(H)=m²−sigma(B). Structural induction proves sigma(B)≤m(m+1)/2, equality for a chain: in the disconnected case strictness is (u−1)(v−1)>0. Connected tree gives Δ≥(h−1)(h−2)/2. Product satisfaction probabilities then show Δ≥h²/9 for every non-Boolean H with equality iff exactly one factor C3 and Boolean factors. Independent direct enumeration through 5 vertices supports the identities; proof covers all finite sizes.
